Asahel Nettleton
AY-suh-hel NET-uhl-tuhn
proper noun (person)
American evangelist (1783-1844) of the Second Great Awakening, defender of doctrinally grounded revival against manipulative "new measures."

Biblical Definition

Asahel Nettleton was an American evangelist of the Second Great Awakening, remarkable both for the depth and durability of his converts and for his principled opposition to the manipulative revivalism that arose in his day. A convinced Calvinist, Nettleton preached the sovereignty of God, the depravity of man, and the necessity of the Spirit's work, and labored with great care for genuine conversions; the fruit of his ministry was notable for its soundness and permanence, with comparatively few of his converts falling away. When Charles Finney introduced the "new measures" — the anxious bench, emotional pressure, and techniques designed to produce immediate decisions — Nettleton opposed them, warning that such methods manufactured false conversions and confused the work of man with the work of God. He insisted that true revival is the sovereign work of the Holy Spirit, not a result that can be engineered by technique. Nettleton stands in the dictionary as the evangelist of sound revival, who labored for conversions wrought by the Spirit and grounded in truth, and who warned the church that manipulation and emotional pressure, however effective at producing decisions, cannot produce the new birth, which is the work of God alone.

Webster 1828 Definition

American evangelist (1783-1844) of the Second Great Awakening; a Calvinist whose converts were notably sound and lasting, who opposed Finney's manipulative "new measures" and insisted that true revival is the sovereign work of the Spirit, not a product of technique.

Key Scripture

John 3:8 — "The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit."

John 1:13 — "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."

Zech 4:6 — "...Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts."

1 Cor 3:7 — "So then neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase."

Modern Corruption

Nettleton's ministry corrects a manipulative revivalism that manufactures decisions by technique, recovering the truth that the new birth is the sovereign, un-engineered work of the Holy Spirit.

expand to see more

Manufactured-decisions correction. The "new measures" Nettleton opposed used emotional pressure and technique to produce immediate decisions, confusing human persuasion with divine regeneration. Nettleton held that the new birth is of God, not of the will of man (John 1:13), and that the Spirit, like the wind, blows where He wills (John 3:8). The dictionary holds that genuine conversion cannot be engineered; decisionism that manufactures professions by manipulation produces false converts, and the church must labor for the Spirit-wrought new birth, not for counted hands.

This entry faces little postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that revival is God's work, not man's technique. "Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit" (Zech 4:6); neither he that plants nor he that waters is anything, but God who gives the increase (1 Cor 3:7). The dictionary commends Nettleton's patient, prayerful, doctrinally grounded labor against every method that trusts in human means to produce what only the Spirit can give, and honors the soundness and permanence of conversions truly wrought by God.
